research_rationale: Executive Order 10717 of June 27, 1957 (22 FR 4632; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10717.txt, read in full) establishes the President's Award for Distinguished Federal Civilian Service (sections 1 and 2), the Distinguished Civilian Service Awards Board and its terms, staff, functions, nominations and criteria (sections 3 to 8, with criteria (a) and (b) under section 8), and an effective date of July 1, 1957 (section 9). Later instruments, each read in its held official text: Executive Order 10979 (26 FR 11937, December 12, 1961) restated sections 2, 7 and 8 (substance changed; recorded before and after in the clause reasons); Executive Order 11085 (28 FR 1759, February 22, 1963) enlarged the Board for Medal of Freedom purposes in its section 3, restricted who sits when recommending recipients of this award, and in its section 2(a) restated section 4 on terms of service; Executive Order 12014 (42 FR 56105, October 19, 1977) abolished the Board, deleted sections 3 to 9 and added new sections 3 and 4 vesting the advising function in the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission; Executive Order 12107 (44 FR 1055, December 28, 1978; effective January 1, 1979 under its section 2-404) in section 2-101 substituted the Office of Personnel Management for the Civil Service Commission and the Director for the Chairman in this order as amended, which changes only the sections added by Executive Order 12014 and no original clause. The Office of the Federal Register disposition note lists these four amendments and no revocation. Sections 1 and 2 remain operative on 2026-10-14: the U.S. Code prints the order as amended (5 U.S.C. 4504 note) and 5 CFR 451.203 implements it. Sections 3 to 9 of the original text ended on October 19, 1977 (section 9, the effective-date clause, was used up when the order took effect on July 1, 1957). Because later amendments restate whole sections, a reviewer should note that section 2 as now in force differs in substance from its 1957 wording. Standing note on sources: the original is held as a machine text layer of the official Federal Register page; check the page before relying on quotations.
savings_reason: Section 4 of Executive Order 12014 and the surviving sections of Executive Order 10717 now work through the Office of Personnel Management; the awards already made under the original sections and the Board's past recommendations have no continuing legal command and nothing was transferred or accrued that the claim relies on. The deleted Board provisions leave no residual effect: the abolition of the Board in Executive Order 12014 and the substitution of the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission (now the Director of the Office of Personnel Management) show the function moved rather than lapsed.
earlier_end_check: Earlier-end check: sections 1 and 2 have no own-term end. For each deleted section the earliest instrument ending it is Executive Order 12014 (October 19, 1977); Executive Orders 10979 and 11085 restated or amended sections 2, 4, 7 and 8 and widened the Board, which are amendments and not ends. Section 9 has an earlier own-terms end on its effective date. No revocation of the whole order appears in the held Federal Register texts, the Office of the Federal Register note, the U.S. Code note or the bounded searches.
scope_check: Scope check: the inventory of eleven clauses (sections 1 to 9 with the two criteria under section 8) is confirmed against the full held text. Partial deletion was checked: Executive Order 12014 deletes sections 3 to 9 only and leaves sections 1 and 2; the later Executive Order 12107 substitution reaches only text that mentions the Civil Service Commission or its Chairman.
independent_command_check: Independent commands: sections 1 and 2 (the award and who may receive it) are independent of the Board sections and continue after the Board was abolished; the new sections 3 and 4 added in 1977 supply the nomination process. The Board sections ended together by deletion.
savings_check: Savings: no appointment, report or transfer is left outstanding by the deleted Board sections that the claim depends on; the awards are presented by the President under sections 1 and 2.

research_rationale: Executive Order 11139 of January 7, 1964 (29 FR 227; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11139.txt, read in full) is a single paragraph. It authorizes the Secretary of Defense (for members of the Army, Navy, Air Force and Marine Corps) and the Secretary of the Treasury (for members of the Coast Guard when it is not operating as a service in the Navy) to prescribe regulations under which the United Nations Medal and Service Ribbon may be accepted by eligible members of the armed forces, and requires that a determination that service in a particular area or for a particular purpose is a justifiable basis for acceptance be made with the concurrence of the Secretary of State. The text states no date, duration, condition or expiry. The only later instrument found is Executive Order 13286 section 68 (68 FR 10619, 10629; effective March 1, 2003 under its section 92), which struck the Secretary of the Treasury and inserted the Secretary of Homeland Security; it is recorded as a later event on the clause. A search of the held Federal Register texts of orders numbered above 11139 for citations of this order found only Executive Order 13286. The Office of the Federal Register disposition note for the order reads that it was amended by Executive Order 13286, February 28, 2003, and names no revocation or supersession. The bounded searches current-law:usc (one hit, the printed Executive Order 13286 note listing section 68 as an amendment of this order), current-law:ecfr (no hit) and later-events:ofr_catalog (one hit, the Executive Order 13286 amendment) show no revocation. The clause is therefore operative on 2026-10-14. No current Code or CFR text printing this order is held, so the current predicate rests on the held original, the held amendment and the three bounded searches (the original_plus_bounded_search route). Standing note on sources: the original is held as a machine text layer of the official Federal Register page; check the page before relying on quotations.
savings_reason: The order grants authority to prescribe regulations and fixes a concurrence requirement; it creates no one-time act that has been performed and used up, and no grant of money or property. No savings or residual effect needs separate treatment: the regulation-making authority and the concurrence rule are the continuing command itself, recorded as operative. No transferred or accrued rights are claimed.
earlier_end_check: Own terms: the single paragraph contains no until-date, expiry, condition or termination. No earlier revocation or supersession was found in the held Federal Register texts of later orders, the Office of the Federal Register note, or the three bounded searches. Executive Order 13286 section 68 is an amendment that substitutes one officer and does not end the clause.
scope_check: Scope: the order is one paragraph with two commands (authority to prescribe regulations for acceptance of the medal and ribbon, and the Secretary of State concurrence rule) that stand or fall together in one sentence structure; the inventory of one clause is confirmed against the full held text. The only later change touches the identity of the Coast Guard's regulation-making officer.
independent_command_check: Independent commands: the concurrence rule for determinations about geographic areas and purposes is part of the same paragraph and no later instrument ends it separately; neither command depends on a deadline or on another order.
savings_check: Savings: no performance, report, appointment or transfer is involved; the authority has not been used up by performance, and nothing was found that ended it.

research_rationale: Executive Order 11155 of May 23, 1964 (29 FR 6909; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11155.txt, read in full) establishes the Commission on Presidential Scholars (section 1), has the Commission choose Presidential Scholars annually under the standards in section 2 (graduating secondary school students chosen for outstanding scholarship, one boy and one girl from each State, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico and a group of territories, plus up to fifteen at large), establishes the Presidential Scholars Medallion (section 3), and has the Office of Education facilitate the order (section 4). The text states no date, duration, condition or expiry. Later instruments, each read in its held official text: Executive Order 12158 (September 18, 1979) added paragraph (5) to section 2 (up to twenty further scholars chosen for outstanding scholarship and demonstrated ability in the visual and performing arts or creative writing), and Executive Order 13697 (80 FR 36691, June 22, 2015) added paragraph (6) to section 2 (up to twenty further scholars for career and technical education); both are recorded as later events on section 2. The Office of the Federal Register note lists these two amendments and no revocation. The U.S. Code prints the order as amended (20 U.S.C. 1221 note). Some words of the original name entities that have since changed or ended (the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare and its Office of Education, the Canal Zone and the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands); no held source shows that these changes ended any command, so every clause is treated as continuing and the changed names are disclosed rather than resolved. All twelve clauses are operative on 2026-10-14. Page check: the original is held as a machine text layer of the official Federal Register issue with location confidence medium; the check of pages 3 and 4 was made on the text layer (page markers, the running head 6910 on the second page, the heading naming the order, the signature of May 23, 1964 and the filing stamp), not on page images, which are not held. Standing note on sources: check the Federal Register pages before relying on quotations.
savings_reason: The order sets up a continuing annual recognition program and medallion; no one-time act in it has been exhausted and nothing was transferred or accrued. No savings or residual effect needs separate treatment.

research_rationale: Executive Order 11858 of May 7, 1975 (40 FR 20263; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11858.txt, read in full) established the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (section 1), assigned data duties to the Secretary of Commerce (section 2), authorized one year of Exchange Stabilization Fund use (section 3), directed agency assistance (section 4), protected confidential information (section 5) and saved other authorities (section 6). Executive Orders 12188 (1980), 12661 (1988, adding sections 7 and 8 on investigations and presidential action), 12860 (1993) and 13286 (2003) amended it, and Executive Order 13456 (January 23, 2008, read in full) amended the order to read as a full restatement. Under the strike-and-insert ruling the clauses that the restatement carries forward continue as amended and the clauses it does not carry forward ended when it took effect. Section 3 ended earlier by its own one-year term. Executive Order 13603 (March 16, 2012) section 803(b) confirms the order as amended remains in effect. The listed Office of the Federal Register amendments were all checked; Executive Order 12977 appears in the dossier chain for this order but its held text does not mention Executive Order 11858 (the cited provision is the Executive Order 13286 amendment), so it is not treated as an amendment. The order is operative on 2026-10-14 as amended.
savings_reason: Section 3 (Exchange Stabilization Fund authority) ended on its own one-year term in 1976 and was later formally removed by the 2008 restatement; no residual effect or transfer needs separate treatment. The 1975 sections ended by the 2008 restatement left no outstanding performance.

research_rationale: Executive Order 11965 of January 19, 1977 (42 FR 4329; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11965.txt, read in full) has four sections: section 1 establishes the Humanitarian Service Medal with ribbons and appurtenances, for award by the Secretary of Defense or, for the Coast Guard when not operating as a service in the Navy, the Secretary of Transportation, and sets eligibility (members of the Armed Forces who after April 1, 1975 distinguished themselves by meritorious participation in a military act or operation of a humanitarian nature); section 2 provides for the design, uniform regulations and order of precedence; section 3 limits the medal to one per person with devices for later participation; section 4 allows posthumous award. The text states no date, duration, condition or expiry. The only later instrument found is Executive Order 13286 section 55 (68 FR 10619, 10629; effective March 1, 2003 under its section 92), which struck the Secretary of Transportation wherever it appears in sections 1, 2 and 4 and inserted the Secretary of Homeland Security; it is recorded as a later event on sections 1, 2 and 4 and does not touch section 3. A search of the held Federal Register texts of orders numbered above 11965 for citations of this order found only Executive Order 13286. The Office of the Federal Register note records only the Executive Order 13286 amendment. The U.S. Code prints the order as amended under 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, part II, chapter 57 note (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09). The three bounded searches show no revocation. All four sections are operative on 2026-10-14. Standing note on sources: the original is held as a machine text layer of the official Federal Register page; check the page before relying on quotations.
savings_reason: The medal remains established and awarded under the order as amended; no one-time act in the order has been exhausted. Section 3 and section 4 are standing rules on the number of medals and posthumous award that continue with the medal. No savings or residual effect needs separate treatment and nothing was transferred or accrued.
earlier_end_check: Own terms: no section contains an until-date, expiry or condition. No earlier revocation or supersession appears in the held Federal Register texts of later orders, the Office of the Federal Register note, the printed U.S. Code note, or the three bounded searches. The one amendment (Executive Order 13286 section 55) substitutes an officer and does not end any section.
scope_check: Scope: the four sections of the held text are the whole order after the heading and before the signature; the dossier's four-clause inventory is confirmed. A partial amendment was checked section by section: Executive Order 13286 section 55 names sections 1, 2 and 4 only.
independent_command_check: Independent commands: sections 1 to 4 are independent in subject (establishment and eligibility; design and regulations; one medal per person; posthumous award), and each is recorded separately; none is a deadline or implementation step that has been performed and used up.
savings_check: Savings: the order establishes a continuing medal; no performance, report or transfer is outstanding or used up.

research_rationale: Executive Order 11990 of May 24, 1977 (42 FR 26961; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11990.txt, read in full) is the wetlands protection order: section 1 directs each agency to minimize destruction of wetlands in land management, construction and land-use activities (excluding permits to private parties on non-Federal property); section 2 requires findings before new construction in wetlands and early public review; section 3 requires budget requests to state accord with the order; section 4 governs disposal of Federally owned wetlands; section 5 lists factors; section 6 requires agency procedures; section 7 defines terms; section 8 states transitional exclusions and an October 1, 1977 implementation date; section 9 excludes emergency work; section 10 allows applicants to assume responsibilities. The only amendment found is Executive Order 12608 section 28 (September 9, 1987), which struck 'and the Water Resources Council' from section 6. The U.S. Code note prints the order as amended and a July 10, 2026 Federal Register proposed rule of the Department of Housing and Urban Development cites it as in force. The order is operative on 2026-10-14.
savings_reason: The order sets continuing duties and definitions for agencies. The only dated provisions are in section 8 (a 1977 cut-off for projects excluded and an October 1, 1977 implementation date), which are transitional and were not used up in a way that ends any command. Nothing was transferred or accrued outside the order.
earlier_end_check: Own terms: no section has an until-date or expiry; the October 1, 1977 date in section 8 is an implementation deadline and an exclusion cut-off, not an end. No earlier revocation or supersession appears in the Office of the Federal Register note, the printed U.S. Code note, or the three bounded searches.
scope_check: Scope: the eighteen clauses of the dossier inventory cover the preamble-free text from section 1 through section 10 and are confirmed against the held text. The one amendment, Executive Order 12608 section 28, touches section 6 only.
independent_command_check: Independent commands: sections 1 to 5 state separate agency commands, section 6 the procedure duty, section 7 definitions, sections 8 to 10 exclusions and an applicant provision; each is recorded as its own clause and none depends on another ending.
savings_check: Savings: the order establishes continuing agency duties; no performance, report or transfer is outstanding or used up beyond the 1977 implementation date, which does not end any command.

research_rationale: Executive Order 12146 of July 18, 1979 (44 FR 42657; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12146.txt, read in full) establishes the Federal Legal Council (section 1-1), states its functions (1-2), requires a litigation notice system (1-3), directs legal disputes between Executive agencies to the Attorney General (1-4), encourages public availability of legal opinions (1-5), provides for automated legal research and information systems (1-6) and sets agency responsibilities (1-7). Executive Order 12608 section 15 (1987) updated the name of the Department of Health and Human Services and Executive Order 13286 section 53 (2003) raised the member limit from 15 to 16 and added the Department of Homeland Security to the initial list. The two-year initial term of section 1-103 ended the initial-membership roster in 1981. The dossier chain lists Executive Order 12977 for this order but the provision it quotes is the Executive Order 13286 section 53 amendment (the held text of Executive Order 12977 does not mention Executive Order 12146), so it is not treated as an amendment. The order is operative on 2026-10-14.
savings_reason: The initial roster ended with the initial term in 1981; the standing provisions of the order are continuing commands. Nothing was transferred or accrued.
earlier_end_check: Own terms: the only time-limited provision is the initial two-year term in section 1-103 (and the one-year report date in section 1-701, a deadline that does not end the order). No earlier revocation or supersession appears in the Office of the Federal Register note or the bounded searches.
scope_check: Scope: the 39 clauses of the dossier inventory cover sections 1-101 to 1-702 including the lettered lists and are confirmed against the held text; the combined printed entry of items (f) and (g) is one clause. Executive Order 13286 section 53 changed section 1-101 and 1-102 only; Executive Order 12608 section 15 changed the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare name.
independent_command_check: Independent commands: the establishment, the roster, the functions of the Council, the litigation notice system, the dispute-submission rule, the legal-opinion encouragement, the research systems and the agency duties are separate commands, each decided on its own.
savings_check: Savings: no performance, report or transfer is outstanding beyond the 1980 and 1981 dates already discussed.

research_rationale: Executive Order 12170 of November 14, 1979 (44 FR 65729; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12170.txt, read in full) finds that the situation in Iran is an unusual and extraordinary threat and declares a national emergency, orders blocked all property and interests in property of the Government of Iran, its instrumentalities and controlled entities and the Central Bank of Iran that are or come within United States jurisdiction or control, authorizes the Secretary of the Treasury to use the powers of the International Emergency Economic Powers Act to carry out the order, and states that the order is effective immediately and is to be transmitted to the Congress and published in the Federal Register. The dossier's single whole-order clause is kept: the four statements are one short instrument and the continuing commands are stated together. The order depends on a declared national emergency, so the held National Emergencies Act continuation notices were checked: the Notice of November 5, 2025 (90 FR 50735) continues for one year the emergency declared in Executive Order 12170 and states that the measures adopted on November 14, 1979 must continue in effect beyond November 14, 2025, which covers 2026-10-14; the held Federal Register full texts also include the November continuation notices of every year from 2007 through 2024 (FR Docs 07-5658, E8-27171, E9-27536, 2010-28780, 2011-29256, 2012-27742, 2013-27376, 2014-27105, 2015-29271, 2016-27033, 2017-24465, 2018-24808, 2019-24806, 2020-25310, 2021-24847, 2022-24779, 2023-25006, 2024-25777). The March notices in the held set (for example 2026-04450) continue the separate emergency declared in Executive Order 12957 and say it is distinct. The Office of the Federal Register note lists as related Executive Orders 12276 to 12284 and 12294 (January and February 1981, implementing the Algiers Declarations) and the annual notices; each of the ten orders was read in its held text: 12276 authorizes escrow arrangements; 12277 to 12281 direct holders (the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, overseas bank branches, domestic banks, non-banking holders, and holders of other property) to transfer identified Iranian Government assets; 12282 revokes the prohibitions in Executive Orders 12205 and 12211 and Proclamation 4702, not Executive Order 12170; 12283 bars prosecution of certain claims against Iran; 12284 restricts transfers of property of the former Shah's estate; 12294 suspends litigation of claims. None of them revokes or supersedes Executive Order 12170; the transfer orders performed a one-time transfer of the identified assets, so the blocking of property that was not so transferred continues, as the November 2025 notice states. 31 CFR part 535 (Iranian Assets Control Regulations) and 31 CFR 560.210 and 211.1 cite the order in the eCFR as of 2026-10-14. The clause is operative on 2026-10-14. Standing note on sources: the original is held as a machine text layer of the official Federal Register page; check the page before relying on quotations. The Federal Register full texts of the continuation notices are held in the packet as federalregister.gov full texts, not as page images.
savings_reason: The January 1981 transfer orders were performed once and moved the identified assets; the blocking of other property of the Government of Iran continues, as the November 5, 2025 notice states that the measures adopted on November 14, 1979 must continue. The immediate-effect and transmittal sentence of the order was a one-time directive carried out at issuance (publication is shown by the Federal Register page of November 15, 1979); it leaves no continuing command and no residual effect needing separate treatment.

scope_check: Scope: the order is four short paragraphs read as one clause. The partial effect of Executive Orders 12277 to 12281 (transfer of identified assets) was checked and recorded as later events; they do not revoke the declaration, the blocking or the Treasury authority.
independent_command_check: Independent commands: the declaration of emergency, the blocking command and the Treasury authorization continue together; the transmittal and publication directive was a one-time act at issuance and the immediate-effect statement was used up when the order took effect on November 14, 1979.
savings_check: Savings: assets transferred in 1981 were transferred in performance; other blocked property remains blocked.

research_rationale: Executive Order 12432 of July 14, 1983 (48 FR 32551; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12432.txt, read in full) has two sections. Section 1 requires Federal agencies with substantial procurement or grantmaking authority to develop minority business enterprise development plans, submit them annually to the Cabinet Council on Commerce and Trade, follow uniform guidelines set by the Secretary of Commerce and the Administrator of the Small Business Administration, report annually, and requires the Secretary of Commerce to report annually to the President. Section 2 requires agencies to establish minority business development programs, to encourage grant recipients to achieve minority business participation, and to give the Cabinet Council information on progress. The text states no date, duration, condition or expiry. The packet inventory missed the end of paragraph 2(c) and paragraph 2(d), which print after the Federal Register page break, so the inventory is corrected to ten clauses (inventory overrides). No amendment, revocation or supersession of the order appears in the held Federal Register texts of later orders (a search of the held texts for citations of this order by number found only regulations and rules that implement or cite it), in the Office of the Federal Register catalog (no disposition note), or in the three bounded searches. The eCFR (48 CFR 1426.7100 and 1426.7102-1; 24 CFR 5.105) and the U.S. Code note under 15 U.S.C. 631 treat the order as continuing. The held sources do not show what body now stands in the place of the Cabinet Council on Commerce and Trade, and none says that an end of the Council ended any command of the order; that open point is disclosed in the clauses that name the Council. All ten clauses are operative on 2026-10-14. Standing note on sources: the original is held as a machine text layer of the official Federal Register page; check the page before relying on quotations.
